shots.title: What a yes/no vote actually does
shots.type: title card, headline + three impact beats + citation footer (v3)

described.Type: title card, headline + three impact beats + citation footer (v3)
described.Content: Headline: "A YES vote keeps Chapter 135 — including the expanded assault-weapons definition." Then three beats: 1. The cutoff: "Owned before Aug 1, 2024? You keep your AR-15. Buying after? Banned outright." 2. Who sits on which side: "Who already owns: white men 48%, nonwhite women 16% (Pew 2017). Who's buying next: 56% of Black non-owners see themselves owning a gun — the highest of any group (Pew 2023)." 3. What the locked-out buyer gets: "The legal alternative fires the same round. The banned 'features' are the adjustability — the stock and grip geometry that lets a smaller shooter fit the rifle." Footer: "Sources: Pew Research 2017/2023 · Acts of 2024, Ch. 135 · mass.gov" plus a QR placeholder (QR composited in the edit, bottom-center, clear of the Reels button stack).

shots.title: The timeline
shots.type: vertical timeline, this is the richest graphic in the cut

described.Type: vertical timeline, this is the richest graphic in the cut
described.Content: Jul 25, 2024 (signed) → Oct 2, 2024 (emergency preamble, "69 days later"; stated reasons "without delay" and time for agencies to prepare) → Oct 23, 2024 (law's own original effective date) → Oct 2024 (93,229 signatures submitted) → Nov 22, 2024 (78,707 verified). Footer note on Article 48's stay.

shots.note: `[source]` citations.md Section 10. The stale render is kept as `images/g10_v2_stale_71days.png`.
